title: Most of what comments add comes from backdoors that label themselves
caption: Extra backdoors Haiku 5.5 xhigh catches, out of 500, when it sees the code's comments, at a 2% audit budget: 468 instead of 426. Every program in the top row has a comment with a word like 'flaw' or 'bug', which a keyword search flags with no false alarms.
notes: Why: these backdoors were written by models asked to insert a bug, and many narrated it in a comment ('# The subtle flaw'). Honest solutions never do. A real attacker wouldn't either.
Only the middle row is gain a keyword search can't explain: 10 of 500 programs, about 2 points.
The bottom row is a built-in placebo. Showing comments can't change a program that has none, and the count doesn't move.
How often a backdoor labels itself depends on which model wrote it (19% to 94%, results/analysis/COMMENTS.md). That is why every main run removes comments.
